sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Funding for the design, implementation, security audit, and adoption of an open-source Cardano development stack led by OpenZeppelin and administered by Intersect.
Recipient: OpenZeppelin for delivery, with Intersect as administrator and recipient of a 3% administration fee.

Deliverables: Three reference implementations: Cardano Liquid Staking Protocol, Self-Repaying Loans Protocol, and Tokenized Money Market Fund., A Cardano contracts library with components including access control, cryptographic utilities, DeFi primitives, governance, credentials, multi-sig/account abstraction, vesting, messaging gateway, and a proposed Cardano Contract ABI., Developer tooling including Contracts Wizard, UI Builder, AI-enhanced development tools, and Cardano documentation., Security retainer of 22 researcher-weeks for audits, full-stack reviews, penetration testing, continuous coverage, AI-security support, and bug bounty assistance., Developer enablement and co-marketing activities including tutorials, workshops, demos, community sessions, and a Cardano network page.
Deadline/expiry: Twelve months in four quarterly milestones from legal contract signing, with milestone dates shown from October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests a total treasury withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada, consisting of 11,443,750 ada for delivery and a 343,313 ada Intersect administration fee.
Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The delivery budget is stated as USD 1,831,000 over 12 months, calculated at a reference rate of USD 0.16 per ada.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal plans a 20% kick-off payment after legal signing and four equal 20% milestone payments released after evidence submission and Intersect Delivery Assurance approval.
Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, high materiality): Funds remaining in the contract at expiry are stated to sweep back automatically to the Cardano Treasury at the contract level.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin proposes to deliver three production-ready reference implementations for liquid staking, self-repaying loans, and a tokenized money market fund.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): OpenZeppelin proposes a secure, audited, documented contracts library for Cardano, with the specific smart contract language to be selected during initial evaluation with ecosystem stakeholders.
missing: Independent evidence for: Funds remaining in the contract at expiry are stated to sweep back automatically to the Cardano Treasury at the contract level.

Independent evidence for: OpenZeppelin claims its existing contracts have supported over $36 trillion in value transferred, $110B+ TVL importing OpenZeppelin Contracts, and about 85% market share in the top 50 DeFi protocols.
Independent evidence for: OpenZeppelin discloses that it has not received ada from the Cardano Treasury within the prior 24 months and has not received Project Catalyst funding.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The proposal requests a total treasury withdrawal of 11,787,063 ada, consisting of 11,443,750 ada for delivery and a 343,313 ada Intersect administration fee." though 1 review blocker(s) remain open.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "Funds remaining in the contract at expiry are stated to sweep back automatically to the Cardano Treasury at the contract level." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: evidence is too thin for a directional vote while 1 blocker(s) remain open.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
